title: The third week
hookLine: walking with Christ through the passion

cards: It's late, in a garden on the Mount of Olives. The supper is over. Jesus takes three of his friends a little way apart and asks them for one thing.
Not to argue his case. Not to fight. Not to find a way out.
Just to stay awake and stay near. Then he goes a short distance further, falls on his face, and prays. When he comes back, they're asleep.
The third week of the Spiritual Exercises begins on nights like this one, and asks the person praying to do what those friends could not.

teach.h: FROM THE SUPPER TO THE TOMB.
teach.b: The third week walks with Christ through the passion: from the supper, through the garden, the arrest, the trials, the cross and the tomb. What's striking is what Ignatius asks the person to want. Not insight.
Sorrow with Christ in sorrow, anguish with Christ in anguish. With is the word that matters. The first week looked at sin, and could feel like standing in the dock.
This is companionship: staying beside someone who is suffering. Ignatius gives a few things to notice. What Christ suffers in his humanity.
How the divinity hides itself: he could stop it, and doesn't. And that he suffers this for me, and what I ought to do and to bear for him.
He even suggests a fast for the imagination: during this week, don't call up joyful thoughts, even good and holy ones like the resurrection.

teach.h: STAY YOU HERE, AND WATCH WITH ME.
teach.b: In the garden, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says to his three friends: "My soul is sorrowful even unto death: stay you here, and watch with me." He didn't ask them to fix anything.
And the Gospel is honest: they slept, more than once. The third week gives the one praying a second chance at that night. Sometimes nobody can make the pain stop.
Staying is still something. And if the pain is your own and feels like too much, you don't have to stay in it alone: in the US, call or text 988, or reach local emergency help.

how: In the third week of an Ignatian retreat, people contemplate the passion scene by scene, from the Last Supper to the burial, asking for the grace of sorrow with Christ in his sorrow.

o: the last week of Lent before Easter
walking with Christ through his passion
a week of fasting from food and joy

games.q: the third week — tap the pairs.
p: walking with Christ through the passion

s: in the third week, Ignatius has people think of the resurrection for comfort
he suggests not calling up joyful thoughts, even holy ones, and staying with the passion.
the grace asked for is sorrow with Christ in sorrow
with is the key word: companionship, not self-blame.
in the garden, Jesus asks his friends to stay and watch with him
he asks them to stay near. the Gospel says they fell asleep.

games.q: you're one of the three friends in the garden. it's late, and Jesus asks you to stay and watch with him. what happens?
o: you stay awake and pray beside him.
you run to warn the others.
games.why: they slept, more than once, and he came back and found them sleeping. the third week gives the one praying a second chance at that night: to stay.

practice: Choose one scene, the garden at night, the road with the cross, or the foot of the cross, and put yourself there quietly, a few steps behind, noticing the faces, the dust, the sounds. Don't try to say anything clever; just stay.
If you pray, ask, as Ignatius does, for sorrow with Christ in his sorrow; if you don't, keep someone who is suffering company in your thoughts.

wordCard.voice: The third week. Walking with Christ through the passion, from the supper to the tomb, asking to stay beside him in his sorrow. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek of Matthew 26:38: keep watch with me.

carryVoice: Your line: suffer with. He asked his friends only to stay. Go gently.

sources.q: My soul is sorrowful even unto death: stay you here, and watch with me.
